common_name: Superbells Holy Moly Calibrachoa (Yellow Million Bells with Cherry-Pink Mottling)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; give it acidic, sharply drained potting mix, since calibrachoa suffers iron chlorosis quickly in alkaline soil.

directions: Superbells Holy Moly is grown for its irregular, splashy mottling rather than a clean pattern: each soft-yellow flower is overlaid with raspberry-pink to cherry-red splotches that vary bloom to bloom, giving the plant a painterly, hand-dabbed look rather than the crisp, symmetric star of Superbells Cherry Star. The habit is a dense, trailing mound that cascades over container rims, and like other calibrachoa the spent flowers shed cleanly without deadheading. Grow in full sun with an acid-forming fertilizer program, and expect the mottling intensity to shift somewhat with temperature, becoming more heavily pink-flushed in cooler weather.
sources: Proven Winners - Superbells Holy Moly Calibrachoa Grower Information
University of Florida IFAS Extension - Calibrachoa for Florida Container Gardens

common_name: Superbells Coralina Calibrachoa (Soft Coral Million Bells with Yellow-Red Eye)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; use acidic, well-drained potting mix and feed with an acid-forming fertilizer to prevent iron chlorosis.

directions: Superbells Coralina bears a much softer, melon-toned coral than the vivid, saturated coral-pink of Superbells Coralberry Punch, with a small sunny yellow-and-red eye at the throat of each bloom that gives the flower more visual depth than a flat single color. The plant forms a mounding, trailing habit well suited to spilling over the edge of a hanging basket or window box. It flowers continuously without deadheading and holds its pastel coloring best with regular but not excessive feeding, since overly high nitrogen pushes foliage at the expense of the delicate flower tone.
sources: Proven Winners - Superbells Coralina Calibrachoa Grower Information
North Carolina State University Extension - Calibrachoa Cultivar Performance Trials

common_name: Superbells Double White Calibrachoa (Fully Double White Million Bells)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; give excellent drainage and acidic potting mix, since calibrachoa roots rot quickly in soggy or alkaline conditions.

directions: Unlike the single, flat, petunia-like blooms typical of the genus, Superbells Double White produces a fully double, ruffled flower with a lacy, rosebud-like texture in clean bright white, giving the plant a richer, more textured look in mixed containers than a standard single-flowered calibrachoa. Growth is a robust, well-branched mounding trailer that quickly re-covers itself with new buds as older flowers shed. Because the extra petal layers add substance to each bloom, this cultivar reads well from a distance as a solid white accent rather than a scattering of tiny flowers, making it a strong choice for pairing with bold, saturated colors in combination plantings.
sources: Proven Winners - Superbells Double White Calibrachoa Grower Information
University of Florida IFAS Extension - Calibrachoa for Florida Container Gardens

common_name: Callie Dark Red Calibrachoa (Deep Ruby-Red Trailing Million Bells)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; the Callie series from Syngenta is bred for compact-to-medium vigor, making it a good fit for smaller hanging baskets and combination pots.

directions: Callie Dark Red is part of Syngenta's Callie breeding line, a separate commercial series from the Proven Winners Superbells already represented in this dataset, and it carries a deep, saturated ruby-red flower color noticeably darker and less orange-toned than most 'red' calibrachoa on the market. Its habit runs slightly more compact than Superbells selections, staying tighter and lower while still trailing enough to soften a container edge. The self-cleaning flowers require no deadheading, and the plant benefits from regular acid-forming fertilizer to sustain the intensity of its dark coloring through the heat of summer.
sources: Syngenta Flowers - Callie Dark Red Calibrachoa Product Information
North Carolina State University Extension - Calibrachoa Cultivar Performance Trials

common_name: Callie Rose Calibrachoa (Pink Trailing Million Bells)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; Callie Rose stays compact, making it useful for smaller pots where a full-size Superbells selection would outgrow the container.

directions: Callie Rose produces clear, warm pink flowers on a compact, trailing plant, sitting in color between the true purple-blue and the yellow selections already common in this genus and filling a distinct rose-pink niche. Its smaller, tighter growth habit compared to the larger Superbells series makes it easier to keep in scale in a small hanging basket or combination planter without constant pinching. Blooms are produced continuously and self-clean without deadheading; regular acid-forming fertilizer and consistent but not soggy moisture keep the color vivid through the growing season.
sources: Syngenta Flowers - Callie Rose Calibrachoa Product Information
University of Florida IFAS Extension - Calibrachoa for Florida Container Gardens

common_name: MiniFamous Uno Double Red Calibrachoa (Double-Flowered Ruby Red Million Bells)
scientific_name: Calibrachoa x hybrida 'MiniFamous Uno Double Red'

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; this Selecta-bred series performs well in both hanging baskets and window boxes thanks to its semi-trailing, floriferous habit.

directions: MiniFamous Uno Double Red is a Selecta One introduction distinct from both the Proven Winners Superbells and Syngenta Callie lines already represented here, and it carries fully double, deep ruby-red flowers that give a fuller, rose-like bloom instead of the typical single petunia-shaped face. Growth is semi-trailing and floriferous, holding up well to wind and rain without the flowers shattering the way many thin-petaled single calibrachoa can. It needs no deadheading and rewards consistent moisture and acid-forming fertilizer with dense, nearly continuous bloom cover from spring through frost.
sources: Selecta One - MiniFamous Uno Series Grower Technical Information
Ball FloraPlant Calibrachoa Brochure

common_name: MiniFamous Neo Double Blue Calibrachoa (Double-Flowered Blue-Purple Million Bells)
scientific_name: Calibrachoa x hybrida 'MiniFamous Neo Double Blue'

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; MiniFamous Neo forms a fuller, rounder mound than the trailing Superbells habit and suits mid-size combination containers.

directions: MiniFamous Neo Double Blue carries fully double, deep blue-purple flowers, distinguishing it both by flower form and depth of color from the single, lighter violet-blue of Superbells Blue already in this dataset. Its semi-trailing habit builds a denser, rounder mound rather than a long cascade, giving it good early-season fullness in a pack or pot before it begins to spill. The doubled flowers hold up well to heat, wind, and rain compared with thinner-petaled single calibrachoa, and the plant needs no deadheading, cleaning itself continuously through the season with regular feeding and acidic, well-drained soil.
sources: Selecta One - MiniFamous Neo Series Grower Technical Information
Ball FloraPlant Calibrachoa Brochure

common_name: Supertunia Vista Paradise Petunia (Watermelon-Pink Vigorous Spreading Petunia)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil; give it the same generous spacing as Supertunia Vista Bubblegum, since it spreads with equal vigor.

directions: Supertunia Vista Paradise carries a distinctive watermelon-pink flower with warm salmon-pink undertones, a softer and more coral-leaning shade than the clear bubblegum pink of Supertunia Vista Bubblegum already in this dataset. Like other Vista-series Supertunias it is exceptionally vigorous, mounding and trailing to fill large containers, hanging baskets, or landscape beds well beyond the footprint of a standard petunia. The flowers are self-cleaning and need no deadheading; a mid-season shearing keeps the planting dense if summer heat causes the stems to become long and sparse.
sources: Proven Winners - Supertunia Vista Paradise Petunia Grower Information
Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder

common_name: Supertunia Vista Snowdrift Petunia (Pure White Vigorous Spreading Petunia)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil, giving ample room since this vigorous white Vista selection spreads well beyond a standard petunia.

directions: Supertunia Vista Snowdrift is a crisp, pure-white-flowered member of the Vista series, filling a clean white niche not otherwise covered among the petunias already in this dataset. It shares the Vista series' exceptional vigor, forming a large mounding, trailing plant capable of covering three to four feet by late season in a landscape bed or covering a full hanging basket on its own. The flowers self-clean without deadheading, and the bright white color makes it a popular unifying color for mixed combination plantings, especially against darker foliage or bolder flower colors.
sources: Proven Winners - Supertunia Vista Snowdrift Petunia Grower Information
Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder

common_name: Supertunia Vista Jazzberry Petunia (Magenta-Purple Vigorous Spreading Petunia)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil; this vigorous magenta Vista selection needs the same generous spacing as its Bubblegum and Silverberry series-mates.

directions: Supertunia Vista Jazzberry produces intensely saturated magenta-purple flowers, a considerably deeper and cooler-toned color than the pastel pink of Supertunia Vista Bubblegum or the silvery lavender of Supertunia Vista Silverberry already cataloged here. It grows with the same outsized vigor typical of the Vista series, mounding upward before trailing widely and quickly filling large containers, hanging baskets, or landscape mass plantings. Blooms continuously from spring to frost without deadheading; the vivid color holds up well in intense summer sun and pairs strongly with chartreuse or silver-foliage companion plants.
sources: Proven Winners - Supertunia Vista Jazzberry Petunia Grower Information
Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder

common_name: Superbena Cobalt Verbena (Dark Blue-Purple Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes; give full sun and good air circulation, since Superbena's mildew resistance still benefits from spacing that keeps foliage drying quickly after rain.

directions: Superbena Cobalt bears dense clusters of dark blue-purple flowers, a noticeably deeper and cooler tone than the wine-red of Superbena Burgundy already in this dataset. The mounding, trailing habit spreads readily as ground cover or spills attractively from a raised container, and the flowers are borne in large, rounded umbels typical of the Superbena breeding line. It flowers continuously from planting to frost without deadheading, tolerates heat and short dry spells once established, and its mildew resistance lets it perform reliably through humid summers where older verbena selections often decline.
sources: Proven Winners - Superbena Cobalt Verbena Grower Information
Louisiana State University AgCenter - Heat-Tolerant Verbena for Gulf South

common_name: Superbena Red Verbena (Rich Red Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes; Superbena Red is somewhat more drought-tolerant than many bedding annuals once its roots establish, and appreciates soil allowed to dry slightly between waterings.

directions: Superbena Red produces clear, rich red flower clusters, a truer and brighter red than the deep wine tones of Superbena Burgundy, distinguishing the two Superbena reds now in this dataset. Growth is mounding and trailing, spreading as an effective groundcover or spilling from a container edge, with large umbels of small flowers typical of the series. It requires less water and fertilizer than many flowering annuals once established, resists deer browsing, and attracts butterflies heavily, blooming continuously without deadheading from planting through the first hard fall frost.
sources: Proven Winners - Superbena Red Verbena Grower Information
Louisiana State University AgCenter - Heat-Tolerant Verbena for Gulf South

common_name: Superbena Cherryburst Verbena (Cherry Red and Peach Striped Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes; expect occasional solid-colored flowers to appear alongside the striped blooms, a normal trait of this novelty-patterned selection.

directions: Superbena Cherryburst is a novelty-patterned selection whose cherry-red flowers are streaked and flamed with soft peach, giving the flower clusters a variegated, hand-painted look unlike any solid-colored verbena already cataloged here. Individual plants may occasionally throw fully solid-red or solid-peach flowers alongside the striped ones, a normal quirk of this pattern rather than a defect. The mounding, trailing habit and mildew resistance match other Superbena selections, blooming continuously from planting to frost with no deadheading required and good tolerance of summer heat and humidity.
sources: Proven Winners - Superbena Cherryburst Verbena Grower Information
Louisiana State University AgCenter - Heat-Tolerant Verbena for Gulf South
